description: A two-panel composite engineering drawing specifying the machining dimensions of the mechanical-test specimens. (a) is a dimensioned technical drawing of a round tensile specimen, drawn horizontally with a dash-dot centreline: cylindrical grip sections of Ø16 mm and length 20 mm at each end, joined to a reduced parallel gauge section of Ø10 mm over a gauge length of 50 mm through fillets marked R10, giving an overall length of 114 mm (all dimensions in mm, as printed). (b) shows the impact specimen as a rectangular bar 50 mm long in elevation plus, to its right, an end-view cross-section 10 mm wide and 10 mm high drawn with hatching; a V-notch of 45° included angle is machined at the mid-length of the 50 mm span, leaving a remaining ligament of 8 mm below the notch (notch depth 2 mm). No material names, compositions, heat-treatment conditions or property values are printed on either panel — the figure defines geometry only. The caption assigns (a) to tensile and (b) to impact testing, and the citing text states the tensile and impact specimens were machined to these dimensions before testing on WDW-200 and JB-300B machines respectively.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a dimensioned engineering drawing of a round tensile specimen with grip diameter Ø16 mm and gauge diameter Ø10 mm.
In (a) the parallel gauge length is marked 50 mm, each grip section is marked 20 mm long, and the overall specimen length is marked 114 mm.
In (a) the transition between grip and gauge section is labelled with a fillet radius R10.
Panel (b) depicts the impact specimen as a rectangular bar of length 50 mm with a square 10 mm × 10 mm cross-section.
In (b) the centre V-notch has a printed included angle of 45° and the hatched cross-section shows a remaining height of 8 mm below the notch.
Neither panel carries any material label, composition, heat-treatment condition or numerical property value; the figure gives specimen geometry only.
The caption states the figure is a schematic of specimens for a) tensile and b) impact tests.
The citing text states tensile tests were performed at room temperature on a universal material testing machine (WDW-200) at a strain rate of 1×10⁻³ s⁻¹ and a tensile speed of 3 mm min⁻¹.

The citing text states YS, UTS, reduction of area (RA) and elongation (A) were determined from the tensile test and that stress–strain curves were corrected by adding real elastic deformation to the plastic deformation.
The citing text states impact toughness was tested on an impact testing machine (JB-300B) to obtain the impact energy (CVN) of the steel samples.

subfigures.description: Dimensioned drawing of a round tensile specimen with a dash-dot centreline: Ø16 mm grip ends of 20 mm length, Ø10 mm gauge section, 50 mm gauge length, R10 fillet, 114 mm overall length; all dimensions labelled in mm.

Impact (Charpy-type) specimen drawing: a 50 mm long rectangular bar in elevation together with a hatched end-view cross-section 10 mm wide × 10 mm high, showing a V-notch with a printed 45° included angle and a remaining ligament of 8 mm below the notch.
